inventory_accounting.unit: distinct inventory callbacks accounted for by the source enumeration; entries are file-qualified

missing_count_unit: entries are per file-qualified callback definition; distinct_names counts callback names
non_claims: The gate proves inventory-vs-source agreement for the registrations this parser can see; it does not prove that every registration in the source was parsed (macro-generated rows and build-script-generated source are outside the parser).

REACHABLE_BOUND is a bound, not a proof. edge-witness records a concrete source call-graph edge from a caller that is itself reachable-bound; module-name-match and unique-name-match rest only on the closure's converged MAY-bound reachable_functions set (unresolved-site-bound/v1, whose own contract says monotonicity is not completeness); dispatcher-row-binding records a STANDARD_EXTS row plus a reachable dispatcher and states that no callback symbol was found in the reachable set.
PROVEN_EXCLUDED carries the written closed-world assumption CE-1; it is a scoped reachability claim about the pinned consumer family, not a property of the callback in general.
The gate does not adjudicate whether an inventoried callback is safe, and it does not change any obligation status.

reconciliation.note: name-prefix matching is not the enumeration; these counts reconcile the six-prefix definition census with the slot-driven manifest and explain why the gate's missing set differs from a raw prefix grep

summary.gate_scope_note: gated = six extension slots + ext_free, source-defined `unsafe fn`, production only; safe extern item functions and imported/macro targets are recorded but are not census-eligible
